If not for that last wicket 39-run stand, things would have looked very bad for New Zealand. Not that 185 is a good total anyway. But hey, we've had weird games at Eden Park. Remember that low scoring thriller in the 2015 WC between New Zealand and Australia? Can the hosts run in hard and get some early wickets to spice this contest up. There sure is a help for the pacers. The Indian new ball bowlers got lateral movement and then generated good bounce. This completely unsettled the NZ batters. Arshdeep got India off to a great start by dismissing Will Young and Henry Nicholls. This set the tone early and Anshul Kamboj operated with laser-like precision. He offered no freebies, even both the ball off the deck and bowled 140kph. Gurnoor enjoyed the bounce on offer.

Daryl Mitchell was determined to steer him team out of trouble but a miscommunication from GP sent him back. After that sharp runout involving Rohit, Virat took a one-handed stunner low to the right at second slip to have his own bit of fun. Arshdeep tried hard to get his second fifer, only ended up leaking 23 runs off his last over. Tickner and Duffy had a lot of fun hitting sixes for fun and Gurnoor was also enjoying his banter with the batters.

[On bowling conditions after coming from the subcontinent] Loving the weather here and there is good purchase off the surface. After coming from the subcontinent, when you get some life in the wickets, it's always a pleasure to bowl here. And yeah, the wind is helping as well. [On New Zealand's frustrating partnership towards the end] I'd say we were being a little greedy and just trying to purchase the wicket. We just need to back what we were doing the whole innings, and the wicket would have come. But we were a little greedy at the end. [On the success with the short ball] I felt like there was something in the wicket, so we were just trying to hit the seam hard and try to get purchase off the surface. And they were trying some shots of that length, so we got the wickets. . [On his celebration] That's for my girlfriend. We do these dance steps when we're out walking or something like that. Whenever the mood is a little low, we cheer each other up with that celebration. So this was for her. [On the target and the chase] I feel like it's a decent total. We just need to bat according to the surface, and we'll see it through.

In a way, the Indian fans who have turned up at the Eden Park today will be happy that NZ stretched the total to 185. They will at least get to see more of their stars with the bat than what it looked like earlier. But here's the interesting bit folks, . Don't write New Zealand off, just yet. India would have asked for the heavy roller and they will hope to take advantage of its effect for the first 8 odd overs where it usually settles the pitch and makes batting slightly easy. Back shortly for the chase...

[On New Zealand's below-par total and India's use of the surface] New Zealand still haven't played overly well. Score slightly flattered by a 39 run partnership late in the piece. Groundstaff are going about their work. I still think it's (pitch) very, very good. Just take a look at how well India did though from a point of view of hitting the surface. I think Tim Seifert's delivery, nice and short, into the wicket, slightly wide of off stump, top edge. They used the bounce really well. And at times in this pitch, it was maybe a little bit of tennis ball-y bounce. When you look at Tom Latham's wicket as well, it's just bounced a little more than he thought and hit the stickers on the bat. [On what New Zealand's bowlers need to do] So therefore, what do New Zealand bowlers need to do? Take a cue a little bit from what India did. They went short into the surface, picked up wickets pretty well with a lot of short balls. They had a hard length as well which created a little bit of doubt in the New Zealand batting lineup. It still looks very, very good. A lot of cross seam deliveries or three-quarter deliveries. They worked really, really well for India. New Zealand need to do the same. Need to get into this attack, this Indian batting lineup very early on. Pick up some wickets. They might get themselves back in the game. But it's a below par score.

Three rain interruptions - one before the start and two during India's chase - but none could dampen the visitors' spirits. Having bowled New Zealand out for a below-par total, India needed a sensible start in the powerplay. Rohit fell in the very first over, but Virat Kohli and Shubman Gill steadied the ship with a crucial 113-run stand for the second wicket. Gill took his time to find his rhythm, but Kohli was in a completely different zone. He looked in sublime touch, peppering the extra-cover and square-leg regions with some delightful strokes. Once past the initial phase, he shifted gears after the first rain break and never really looked back until a Duffy short ball brought his entertaining knock to an end in the 20th over. India did lose four wickets in quick succession towards the end, but with fewer than 30 runs needed, the result was never really in doubt. This was Kohli at his vintage best - composed when the situation demanded, ruthless when the opportunity presented itself, and completely switched on in the field, where he also pouched a couple of catches. Another day, another reminder of why he remains the ultimate chase master! A thoroughly professional performance from India, with Kohli once again stealing the show. Stick around for the post-match reactions...

[On the key to his outstanding figures of 2 for 22 in 10 overs] I think the key was just consistent length and line, not thinking about how the wicket is behaving, just the basic plan, bowling on right lines and right areas. [On using variations in seam position] I think the wobble seam ball was working very well, so I was using that again and again. [On his preparations for the series] Just working on lengths and good lines, and just looking at the strengths and weaknesses of the batsmen and just working on that. [On adjusting his length to the conditions in New Zealand] No, it doesn't matter, because I also get a good amount of bounce off the wicket as well. So it's like it's only about the length which I am bowling, just focusing on that. [On assessing conditions at different venues] You just have to look at the wicket and see what is happening on the wicket, what is the best ball to bowl, what is the right length to bowl, just focus on that.

: [On New Zealand's batting performance] Yeah, I think the pitch probably bounced and, you know, it was probably a little bit faster than we kind of expected at Eden Park. I think we just probably didn't adapt as quick as we could. And with some good bowling from India as well. [On the challenge of adapting to the bounce at Eden Park] Yeah, I think when you try to fight the bounce at Eden Park, it can be quite hard. I think the way they kind of used it a little bit more and, Shreyas was trying to go more fine with the shorter balls. And yeah, obviously bounced a lot and after the rain it kind of skidded on nicely. So yeah, a few short balls out there. [On the bowling unit's response after a difficult start] Yeah, very happy. It was easy for us to kind of roll over there after the start they got. So credit to the fast bowlers to keep backing it up. So yeah, I think we found some good stuff at the end of the game there and we can kind of go on to Wellington.

: [On India's bowling and fielding performance] I think we were very good with the bowling. And I think our fielding was also really good. That run out by Rohit bhai, I think changed the momentum of the game. I think it was really that partnership (Mitchell & Phillips), we saw that even in India - those two batted really well in India. And overall I think a very good team performance for us. [On Anshul Kamboj and Gurnoor Brar's performances] I mean Anshul is the kind of a bowler, I think he's tailor-made for these kind of conditions, always nippy, trying to seam the ball. And good with the old ball. We felt when there's not much happening from the wicket, he (Brar) can create that extra bounce and with his pace and the way both of them bowled tonight was really magnificent to watch. [On adapting to the conditions during the rain interruptions] I mean it's never easy when you are set and then it rains and the wicket got a little bit quick, it got a little bit more nippy after the rain. So the target reduced. So we were just trying to play our normal cricket. And I think the way Virat bhai batted, it made things a lot more easy for us. [On areas to work on ahead of the Wellington game] Nothing really, if we are able to replicate our performance, it's all about consistency for us. If we are able to do the same thing over and over again, I think we'll be in a great space.

Just like the T20Is, India have kicked off the five-match ODI series with a win. Can they carry this momentum into Wellington when the two sides meet again on Saturday? New Zealand, meanwhile, have been hampered by a couple of injury concerns but will be hoping to have their key players fit and firing for the next encounter.
